# A variable of a defined option type keeps the declaration's type:
# lib.Default is lib.MaybeInt, not lib.MaybeInt?. The anonymous option
# around a named payload still restores as before.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

cd src
logos build ./...
logos lint ./...
logos run ./cmd
stderr '^ok$'
stderr '^cur nil$'
cd neg
! logos build ./...
stderr 'cannot use'
cd ..

logos eject -o out
exists out/cmd/main.go
cd out
exists $UPROOT1272/bin/go
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
exec $GOROOT/bin/gofmt -l .
! stdout .
cd ../..

-- src/go.mod --
module example.com/optdefined

go 1.27

-- src/lib/lib.lgo --
package lib

type MaybeInt int?

var Default MaybeInt

type User struct {
	Name string
}

var Current User?

-- src/cmd/main.lgo --
package main

import "example.com/optdefined/lib"

func takeMaybe(v lib.MaybeInt) lib.MaybeInt {
	return v
}

func main() {
	var local lib.MaybeInt = lib.Default
	var back lib.MaybeInt = takeMaybe(local)
	_ = back
	println("ok")
	if lib.Current == nil {
		println("cur nil")
	}
}

-- src/neg/go.mod --
module example.com/optdefinedneg

go 1.27

require example.com/optdefined v0.0.0

replace example.com/optdefined => ..

-- src/neg/neg.lgo --
package neg

import "example.com/optdefined/lib"

// Default stays an option: assigning it to int must not compile.
var _ int = lib.Default
